title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E02 — The Major Museums of Cairo
Using objects from Cairo's three great museums; tracing 5,000 years of Egyptian history; Narmer Palette sets the conventions for Egyptian art; what a statue of King Khafre and Tutankhamun's golden throne tell about Egypt from various periods.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E03 — How to Build a Pyramid
The origins of the Egyptian pyramids; the symbolism of their architectural form; the methods of pyramid building; the pyramids' orientation to the cardinal points; the techniques of construction; the funerary rituals that accompany royal interments.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E04 — The Great Pyramid: The Last Ancient Wonder
Khufu, builder of the Great Pyramid; the engineering and administrative feat of the construction; pyramid's network of internal passages and funerary chambers; how the burial chambers are sealed; the royal necropolis complex that adjoins the pyramid.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E05 — The Great Sphinx and the Giza Plateau
The stunning monuments of the Giza Plateau; the pyramid complex of Khafre and its remarkable necropolis; the legendary Sphinx; the Sphinx Temple and the tomb of Queen Meresankh; the pyramid complex of Menkaure; the Lost City of the pyramid builders.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E06 — The Step Pyramid: Djoser's Stairway to Heaven
King Djoser's Step Pyramid complex at Saqqara; how a traditional mastaba tomb is transformed into the famous Step Pyramid; the 37-acre complex; its courtyards and underground tombs and galleries; their extraordinary architectural features and decor.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E07 — The Capital at Memphis and the Saqqara Tombs
Exploring Memphis, Ancient Egypt's great capital; the Temple of Ptah; its remarkable statuary and cult structures; the Necropolis of Saqqara; the artistic riches of the Pyramid of King Unas; the Tomb of the Two Brothers; the Tomb of Nefer and Kahay.

title: The Great Tours: A Guided Tour of Ancient Egypt
description:
S01 E08 — Old, New, and Late Saqqara
The New Kingdom cemetery, containing mastaba tombs with unparalleled relief carvings; the Pyramid of King Teti; the spectacular tombs of his officials, Mereruka and Kagemni, with their exquisitely carved decoration; a visit to the Serapeum.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E01 — George Washington's Doubts
Explaining the importance of getting a well-rounded understanding of the Founders; Professor Guelzo explores Washington's fears about post-Revolutionary America; Washington's concerns about how people could administer their own affairs.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E02 — Thomas Mifflin's Congress
Before the ratification of the Constitution, there are presidents of the Congress created by the Articles of Confederation; the failures of one president, Thomas Mifflin, offer a window into the problems facing the United States of America in 1783.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E01 — The Many Faces of Jesus
Scholars who have devoted their lives to studying the ancient sources about Jesus come to varying conclusions; seeing what can be learned about what Jesus most likely says and does by working from a strictly historical perspective.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E02 — One Remarkable Life
Beginning the study of the historical Jesus by examining the world within which the Christian religion is born; this world is largely populated by "pagans" who, unlike the Jews and then later the Christians, believe not in one but in many gods.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:

Start the course on the U.S. Constitution by learning about the English culture that inspired American law and the conflict with England that caused the revolution.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E02 — Failures of Early American Governments
Consider where the Articles of Confederation came from.

description:

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Birth of Christianity
This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — The Religious World of Early Christianity
This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — The Historical Jesus
In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E01 — The Historical Study of Christianity
The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E02 — The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E03 — The First Cultural Context - Judaism
The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E04 — The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E05 — Paul and Christianity's First Expansion
Observing how Christianity's expansion happens; the broad adaptations it makes in a relatively short period; investigating the role of Paul's letters as a primary record of the convictions, culture, practices and troubles of the early Christians.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E06 — The Diversity of Early Christianity
Influences in early Christianity beyond Jesus and Paul; the differences in conviction and perspective in the gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John; the four Gospels' interpretations of Jesus's role; their convergence on the nature of his character.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E01 — The Many Faces of Jesus
Scholars who have devoted their lives to studying the ancient sources about Jesus come to varying conclusions; seeing what can be learned about what Jesus most likely says and does by working from a strictly historical perspective.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E02 — One Remarkable Life
Beginning the study of the historical Jesus by examining the world within which the Christian religion is born; this world is largely populated by "pagans" who, unlike the Jews and then later the Christians, believe not in one but in many gods.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E03 — Scholars Look at the Gospels
The work of German writer D. F. Strauss argues that the Gospels are best understood as containing history-like stories that intend to convey truth but do not occur as they are narrated, which is why most scholars find his approach illuminating.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E04 — Fact and Fiction in the Gospels
Scholars question the historical accuracy of some gospel accounts not out of hostility toward Christianity, but because of historical evidence; what this evidence is; how historians assess it.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E05 — The Birth of the Gospels
Before the Gospels, accounts of Jesus are passed on by word of mouth; whether it is possible to move "behind" the written accounts to learn more about this original oral tradition, and perhaps even about Jesus himself as a historical person.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E06 — Some of the Other Gospels
In addition to the New Testament, other written sources about Jesus come down from antiquity; what these other, noncanonical Gospels are like; considering their origins and sources; how much they can reveal about what Jesus actually says and does.

Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E05 — Paul and Christianity's First Expansion
Observing how Christianity's expansion happens; the broad adaptations it makes in a relatively short period; investigating the role of Paul's letters as a primary record of the convictions, culture, practices and troubles of the early Christians.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E06 — The Diversity of Early Christianity
Influences in early Christianity beyond Jesus and Paul; the differences in conviction and perspective in the gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John; the four Gospels' interpretations of Jesus's role; their convergence on the nature of his character.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E01 — The Many Faces of Jesus
Scholars who have devoted their lives to studying the ancient sources about Jesus come to varying conclusions; seeing what can be learned about what Jesus most likely says and does by working from a strictly historical perspective.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E02 — One Remarkable Life
Beginning the study of the historical Jesus by examining the world within which the Christian religion is born; this world is largely populated by "pagans" who, unlike the Jews and then later the Christians, believe not in one but in many gods.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E03 — Scholars Look at the Gospels
The work of German writer D. F. Strauss argues that the Gospels are best understood as containing history-like stories that intend to convey truth but do not occur as they are narrated, which is why most scholars find his approach illuminating.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E04 — Fact and Fiction in the Gospels
Scholars question the historical accuracy of some gospel accounts not out of hostility toward Christianity, but because of historical evidence; what this evidence is; how historians assess it.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E05 — The Birth of the Gospels
Before the Gospels, accounts of Jesus are passed on by word of mouth; whether it is possible to move "behind" the written accounts to learn more about this original oral tradition, and perhaps even about Jesus himself as a historical person.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E06 — Some of the Other Gospels
In addition to the New Testament, other written sources about Jesus come down from antiquity; what these other, noncanonical Gospels are like; considering their origins and sources; how much they can reveal about what Jesus actually says and does.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Birth of Christianity
This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — The Religious World of Early Christianity
This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — The Historical Jesus
In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E01 — The Historical Study of Christianity
The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E02 — The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E03 — The First Cultural Context - Judaism
The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation

S01 E04 — The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E01 — Needing No Introduction?
Mark Twain is a celebrity of almost mythic status; explaining the origin of Samuel Clemens's famous pseudonym; asking what Mark Twain means to his American audience and to the man who creates him.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E02 — From Samuel Clemens to Mark Twain
Seeing Twain's life as one of milestones; the financial success brought by his literary triumphs is at times disrupted by disastrous investments such as the Paige typesetting machine; Twain's happy married life is hit by several family tragedies.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E03 — The Sense of Mark Twain's Humor
Twain says that as a humorist, "I have always preached."; his sermon consists of "cracking up" idols of reverence to make room for truth; his speech about the "cannibals" of the Sandwich Islands shows him tickling the audience's funny bones.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E04 — Marketing Twain
Concerning his writing, Twain once confesses that the motive of profit has an importance "almost beyond my own comprehension."; exploring why money means so much to Twain; detailing the marketing schemes he uses to maximize his income.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E05 — Innocents Abroad, I-Going East
Henry Ward Beecher organizes Twain's trip East as a pilgrimage to pay obeisance to the founding monuments of Western culture; how Twain turns the tables; whether Twain is psychologically preparing America for its role as a world power.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E06 — Innocents Abroad, II-Traveling to Unlearn
Twain's goal in "Innocents Abroad" is to teach his readers to see the Old World with their own eyes, asking what of value can remain after everything is mocked into submission when Twain trains his wit on the holy sites of the Bible.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E07 — Roughing It-Going West
Twain mines his own past as a prospector and turns it into comic frontier fiction in "Roughing It"; the work also marks Twain's first prominent use of American vernacular language; his intimation that it deserves a place in American literature.

title: The Life and Work of Mark Twain
description:
S01 E08 — The Lecture Tours
Despite the rigors of touring and the limitations imposed by his audiences' tastes, Twain comes to love the thrill of live lecturing; he skillfully blends the serious academic content that audiences demand with his own trademark sardonic wit.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E01 — Meeting the Norse Gods of the Viking Age
The Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda chronicle the lives of the Norse gods of the Viking Age.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E02 — Fate and the Norse Worldview
Insight into the profound Norse sense of fatalism and the importance of reckless courage.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E03 — The Norse Art of Mythic Storytelling
A comparison of two versions of a story to highlight the dream logic inherent to Norse mythology.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E04 — The Norse Gods Are Characters with Flaws
An in-depth understanding of different shades of the personalities of the Norse gods.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E05 — The Norse Creation: Dawn of Strife
Discovering how the Norse creation myth begins and ends.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E06 — First Humans, the Nine Realms, and Yggdrasil
A broader look at the Norse mythos and humanity's place within it.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E07 — Loki and His Children
The story of Loki, a complicated figure who lives alongside the gods but compulsively troubles them.

title: Norse Mythology
description:
S01 E08 — Balder's Death: Tragic Murder of a God
One of the two different versions of the story of Balder's death omits the presence of Loki.
